entries.subject: Stellar and planetary measurements
entries.finding: Luque et al. (2023), Nature 623, 932–937, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06692-3, Table 1: radius 2.388 +/- 0.036 Earth radii, using 6378.137 km per Earth radius. Only a mass upper limit is published; GM=0 marks no adopted mass, not a massless planet. No oblateness is measured; the rendered shape is a sphere. Circular orbits with the published 2023 periods and transit epochs. Planet-planet perturbations and transit-timing variations are not propagated; this is not a current transit forecast or an N-body resonance simulation. Absolute sky nodes and spin axes are unknown.

entries.subject: Surface colour, map and rotation
entries.finding: The selected transit/RV evidence supplies a radius and orbit, not a resolved surface, colour or spin. Neutral gray and a fixed display axis are conventions.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-backed resolved product, rotational constraint or appropriate photometric model becomes available.
